projects.name: East Lansing MISS DIG Failure
projects.description: A cable crew installing Zayo fiber ruptured an unmarked Consumers Energy gas main in East Lansing after USIC, Consumers' locating contractor, failed to mark it.
projects.detail: On June 3, 2021, workers from 2-D Aerial Cable Construction laying cable for Zayo ruptured a Consumers Energy gas main near Forest and Fern streets in East Lansing. The crew said it repeatedly had to call MISS DIG because lines were reported marked or clear when they were not; USIC, hired by Consumers to mark lines, had not marked this one. The 2-inch main was clamped about three hours later and Consumers spent several days on repairs. In January 2020 Consumers had paid $545,000 in a settlement with Attorney General Dana Nessel over failures to mark gas lines after receiving dig notices.
projects.timeline: June 3, 2021; main clamped ~3 hours later, repairs over several days

projects.name: NIPSCO Locate Failure Pattern (Indiana)
projects.description: NIPSCO fined $463,400 after 190 instances of failing to accurately locate underground gas facilities for excavators in 2024.
projects.detail: Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission fined NIPSCO $463,400 for 190 instances in 2024 where the utility failed to timely or accurately locate its underground gas facilities when excavators requested information through Indiana 811. The violations placed NIPSCO in penalty level 4, the second-highest classification. While NIPSCO responded to over 565,000 locate requests with 99.96% accuracy, each failure created potential for catastrophic dig-in incidents.

projects.name: Fayetteville Bragg Blvd Gas Strike
projects.description: NCDOT subcontractor struck a 12-inch gas main during median excavation, forcing a 21-hour repair and extended road closure on a major commercial corridor.
projects.detail: On January 5, 2024, a subcontractor for NCDOT working on a Bragg Boulevard median project used an excavator to dig in the median and struck a 12-inch Piedmont Natural Gas main. Bragg Boulevard was closed from Swain Street to Sycamore Dairy Road. It took 21 hours for Piedmont Natural Gas to cap the ruptured line. Businesses along the major commercial corridor were forced to close, and residents in surrounding areas were evacuated.
projects.budget: $4.2M road project → $4.55M with damage and delays

projects.name: Sellersburg Fiber Utility Strikes
projects.description: Lumos fiber installation crews repeatedly struck gas and water lines in a subdivision, shutting off gas to 200 customers and flooding streets; work permits suspended twice.
projects.detail: Lumos crews installing fiber optic lines in the Yorktown Park subdivision in Sellersburg hit a main gas line in September 2025, causing a leak that shut off service for approximately 200 customers and diverted traffic on State Road 60. Additional water line strikes occurred on December 23, 2024 and January 12, 2026. Floyd County suspended Lumos work permits twice due to safety concerns.
projects.budget: Fiber installation → $250K+ in utility repairs and road damage
projects.timeline: 2024 start → Work permits suspended multiple times through 2026

projects.name: Platte City Fiber/Gas School Evacuation
projects.description: United Fiber boring subcontractor struck two natural gas lines near schools, forcing emergency evacuation of elementary and high school students.
projects.detail: On August 29, 2025, a subcontractor boring underground for United Fiber's internet project struck two Liberty Utilities natural gas lines on Thomas Drive and Bent Oak Court near Siegrist Elementary and Platte County High School. Students from both schools were evacuated. Platte City suspended all United Fiber right-of-way permits indefinitely pending review.
projects.budget: Fiber installation → $300K+ in emergency response and delays
projects.timeline: Aug 29, 2025 → Operations resumed after review Sep 2025

projects.name: Sebring Fiber Gas Line Strikes
projects.description: Fiber optic crew struck two separate gas lines within blocks of each other, forcing evacuation of 20 homes during an approaching thunderstorm.
projects.detail: On April 17, 2026, a crew installing fiber optic cable in Sebring hit two gas lines in quick succession on Oregon Street and a block away. Twenty homes were evacuated. The situation became especially dangerous as a strong thunderstorm with lightning approached the village while gas was still leaking. Power was temporarily cut to the entire village as a precaution.
projects.budget: Fiber installation → $100K+ in emergency response and repairs

projects.name: Palm Bay Water Reclamation Facility
projects.description: Wastewater treatment plant expansion plagued by unexpected subsurface conditions and contractor default after 5.5 years still unfinished.
projects.detail: Palm Bay's South Regional Water Reclamation Facility was budgeted at $21.36 million with a June 2022 completion date. Unexpected site conditions discovered during construction required significant modifications. Change orders pushed total cost to $24.91 million. The city default-terminated general contractor RJ Sullivan and voted to approve a completion agreement with the project's surety company. The facility remained non-functional as of mid-2026.

projects.name: Perry Township US-20 Widening Gas Strike
projects.description: Road-widening crew struck an Enbridge gas pipeline, causing a fire that burned for over an hour with flames reaching electrical lines; two homes evacuated.
projects.detail: On June 28, 2026, a construction crew widening North Ridge Road (US Route 20) in Perry Township struck an Enbridge gas pipeline. The crew's utility truck caught fire, with flames extending to the tops of electrical lines. Firefighters allowed the fire to burn for over an hour until Enbridge crews shut off the gas. This was the third gas-line incident in Northeast Ohio within 24 hours.
projects.budget: US-20 widening project → $200K in delays and damage

projects.name: Wappingers Falls Gas Explosion
projects.description: Central Hudson contractors struck an unmarked gas line during routine maintenance, causing an explosion that collapsed a building and injured 15 people; $5M penalty plus $3.5M safety fund.
projects.detail: On November 2, 2023, Central Hudson Gas & Electric contractors performing gas line replacement work struck an unmarked 3/4-inch gas service line at 4 Brick Row using an excavator. The explosion collapsed a multi-family brick building, injuring 10 civilians (including 2 children) and 5 first responders. The NY Public Service Commission found Central Hudson had actual knowledge of the active line but failed to include it in the project binder. Central Hudson was ordered to pay a $5 million penalty and establish a $3.5M gas safety remediation fund.
projects.budget: Maintenance work → $8.5M in penalties and remediation

projects.name: Deer Park Pipeline Fire
projects.description: Vehicle struck an above-ground Energy Transfer pipeline valve, causing a massive explosion and fire that burned for four days, damaging five homes and forcing evacuation of 1,000+ residences.
projects.detail: On September 16, 2024, a vehicle drove through a fence and struck an above-ground valve on a 20-inch Energy Transfer NGL pipeline on Spencer Highway in Deer Park. The explosion sent flames hundreds of feet into the air. Nearly 1,000 homes in La Porte and about 50 in Deer Park were evacuated, plus San Jacinto College. The fire burned for four days. The Texas Railroad Commission reported $1.3 million in property damage. The fire emitted 330,621 pounds of VOCs during a 10-hour period.
projects.budget: Pipeline operations → $1.3M in property damage per TRC

projects.name: Lansing Hospital Gas Strike
projects.description: Gas line struck during Michigan Avenue road construction, forcing evacuation of two UM Health-Sparrow hospital buildings including a cancer center.
projects.detail: On September 9, 2025, a gas line was struck during the Michigan Avenue construction project in Lansing, forcing the evacuation of the UM Health-Sparrow Professional Building and the Herbert-Herman Cancer Center. Consumers Energy, Lansing Fire Department, and Lansing BWL responded. The main hospital and emergency room remained open. By noon, both evacuated buildings were cleared for reoccupation.
projects.timeline: Sept 9, 2025; buildings cleared for reoccupation by noon

projects.name: Philadelphia Ogontz Gas Main Rupture
projects.description: Danella Construction excavator struck a 20-inch cast iron gas main during PGW pipeline work, forcing evacuation of 3,000+ people including Central High School.
projects.detail: On February 27, 2025, a Danella Construction excavator struck a 20-inch cast iron gas main at West Olney Avenue and 18th Street in Philadelphia's Ogontz section. The six-inch crack sent methane clouds into the air, forcing evacuation of over 3,000 people including students from Central High School, Philadelphia High School for Girls, and La Salle University. The struck main was a legacy pipe already scheduled for replacement, highlighting PGW's $4.5 billion deferred infrastructure backlog.

projects.name: Morningside Heights Gas Main Strike
projects.description: Excavation crew fractured a 20-inch high-pressure gas main on Broadway near Columbia University, evacuating seven buildings and suspending No. 1 subway service.
projects.detail: On April 30, 2025, an excavation crew struck and fractured a 20-inch high-pressure gas main on Broadway near West 122nd Street. Seven buildings were evacuated including the Manhattan School of Music. MTA suspended No. 1 train service between 96th Street and 168th Street in both directions. Con Edison capped the leak within about an hour.

projects.name: Bronx Bedford Park Gas Main Rupture
projects.description: Gas main erupted at Bedford Park Boulevard and Webster Avenue, sending a mustard-colored plume over the Bronx and injuring five people; 600+ residents lost gas service.
projects.detail: On September 22, 2024, a gas main ruptured near Bedford Park Boulevard and Webster Avenue in the Bronx. The eruption sent a visible mustard-colored substance into the air that could be smelled for miles. Over 100 firefighters responded, evacuating apartment buildings and 200 parishioners from St. Mary's Orthodox Church. Five people were treated, three transported to hospitals. Over 600 residents lost gas service.

projects.name: National City Plaza Bonita Gas Explosion
projects.description: Construction crew severed a gas line while digging for a new water line at Westfield Plaza Bonita Mall, causing a 15-20 foot fireball that engulfed heavy equipment.
projects.detail: On July 31, 2024, a construction crew working at Westfield Plaza Bonita Mall in National City accidentally severed a large natural gas line while digging for a new water line. The explosion caused flames shooting 15-20 feet into the air, engulfing both a Bobcat and an excavator. The mall was evacuated. SDG&E crews spent all day restoring gas service.
projects.budget: $5.5M water line installation → $6.3M with equipment loss

projects.name: Portland Airport Way Gas Rupture
projects.description: Horizontal drilling machine ruptured a gas pipe near NE 138th and Airport Way, closing westbound lanes and triggering building evacuations.
projects.detail: On April 8, 2024, a horizontal drilling machine ruptured a natural gas pipe near Northeast 138th and Airport Way in Portland. Portland Fire & Rescue evacuated nearby buildings. NW Natural clamped the ruptured line at approximately 4:50 p.m. The access hole in the westbound lanes of NE Airport Way caused an extended road closure.

projects.name: Seattle Eastlake Ave Gas Strike (RapidRide J)
projects.description: Construction crews hit a gas line on Eastlake Avenue during $128.5M RapidRide J Line corridor work, closing all lanes and triggering emergency response.
projects.detail: On January 6, 2026, construction crews hit a gas line at Eastlake Avenue E and E Roanoke Street during work on the $128.5 million RapidRide J Line corridor project. All northbound and southbound lanes were blocked before 5 a.m. Seattle police, fire, and Puget Sound Energy responded. SDOT had implemented potholing measures learned from RapidRide G, but the strike still occurred.

projects.name: Waterbury CT Transmission Main Failure
projects.description: Catastrophic failure of a 55-year-old 42-inch transmission main left 100,000 people without water, triggering a $13M emergency rehabilitation project.
projects.detail: In December 2025, a 42-inch, 55-year-old transmission main burst with explosive force on Thomaston Avenue in Waterbury, launching pavement into the air and shattering windows. The failure was preceded by a September 2025 break of a 100-year-old 30-inch main that cost $500,000-$600,000. The December break left approximately 100,000 people without water, closing schools and restaurants. Emergency rehabilitation of nearly two miles of critical infrastructure cost about $13 million.
projects.budget: $30M water system program → $43M+ with emergency rehabilitation
projects.timeline: Mar 2025 start → Jan 2026 emergency completion (4 months added)

projects.name: Lake Worth Beach Sewer Force Main Rupture
projects.description: AT&T fiber optic directional drilling struck a 36-inch sewer force main, spilling 6 million gallons of raw sewage into the canal system.
projects.detail: During an AT&T fiber optic expansion project in Palm Beach County, directional drilling struck a critical 36-inch sewer force main along Florida Mango Road at 16 feet below ground. The rupture discharged approximately 6,050,000 gallons of raw sewage into the L-10 Canal, caused the road to cave in, and triggered over $7.5 million in damage claims. The incident spawned two lawsuits including an insurance coverage dispute.

projects.name: Kinder Morgan Wyoming Pipeline Rupture
projects.description: Kinder Morgan natural gas pipeline ruptured along I-80, sparking a massive fire visible 60 miles away that charred a freight train.
projects.detail: On September 21, 2025, a Kinder Morgan Colorado Interstate Gas Company pipeline ruptured along Interstate 80 west of Cheyenne, igniting a massive fire visible from Loveland, Colorado — over 60 miles away. A Union Pacific freight train was halted within 40 feet of the blaze; its cars were blackened. The fire burned for nearly eight hours. NTSB investigators were dispatched and the pipeline segment was shut down.
projects.budget: Pipeline operations → $5M+ damage and lost throughput

projects.name: Seattle Ship Canal Water Quality Tunnel
projects.description: CSO tunnel budget grew from $423M to $710M after tunnel diameter increased, megaboulders encountered underground, and digging took 10 months longer than planned.
projects.detail: Originally estimated at $423 million in 2014, the cost rose to $570 million when tunneling began and eventually reached $710 million. The tunnel diameter was increased by nearly 5 feet for climate resilience. A megaboulder slowed the tunnel boring machine. COVID-19 complications extended digging by 10 months. Design refinements added another $47 million.

projects.name: Denver FasTracks Rail Expansion
projects.description: Voter-approved $4.7B transit expansion encountered utilities dating to the mid-19th century with no accurate records, ballooning to $7.4B with four rail lines still unfinished after 20 years.
projects.detail: Approved by voters in 2004 at $4.7 billion with all lines complete by 2017, the program has spent $5.5 billion completing only 75% of planned work. Construction encountered underground utilities dating back to the mid-1800s with no accurate records. Franchise agreements put utility relocation on providers but did not align with the project schedule. RTD estimates $1.6 billion more is needed, with full completion projected for 2034-2044.

projects.name: Cincinnati Connector Streetcar
projects.description: Underground utility relocation costs far exceeded estimates along the 3.6-mile loop, with 17 utilities in the right-of-way and unknown utilities discovered with no owner.
projects.detail: The streetcar cost $148 million versus an original estimate of approximately $100 million. Utility relocation began in February 2012 and proved far more expensive than planned. Agreements with 17 utilities in the right-of-way took longer than scheduled. Unknown utilities were discovered during construction with no utility company claiming ownership. The streetcar opened in September 2016.

projects.name: Norfolk Tide Light Rail
projects.description: Downtown utility relocations proved far more complex than anticipated, requiring entirely new duct bank systems; costs jumped from $232M to $314M.
projects.detail: Downtown CBD utilities were so old and repeatedly modified that standard relocation was impossible, requiring construction of entirely new duct bank systems. Utility relocations in the Norfolk Southern right-of-way took far longer than scheduled because the complexity was not adequately understood. The system opened 18 months late on August 19, 2011, at a final cost of $314 million.

projects.name: Atlanta CSO Tunnel Program
projects.description: Atlanta's consent decree sewer tunnel system cost over $4 billion — double original estimates — encountering extensive underground utility conflicts with century-old infrastructure.
projects.detail: Since 1999, Atlanta has invested over $4 billion on consent decree compliance, roughly double original estimates. The West Area CSO Tunnel alone cost over $400 million. Construction of deep shafts and miles of tunnel in a dense urban environment with aging 100+ year-old infrastructure created extensive utility conflicts. Modified consent decrees repeatedly extended timelines.

projects.name: Lynnwood Link Light Rail Extension
projects.description: 8.5-mile light rail extension ran $500M over budget as property acquisition for utility corridors surged 44% and construction bids escalated.
projects.detail: Sound Transit announced in 2017 the extension would cost $500 million more than expected. Property acquisition for utility corridors and station infrastructure surged by $101 million to $236 million. Design scope increased $150-190M. Construction market costs soared — masonry doubled and escalator costs quadrupled. Service began August 30, 2024, roughly a year late.

projects.name: Green Line Extension (GLX Somerville)
projects.description: MBTA light rail extension saw costs balloon from $1.3B to $2.28B after underestimated utility relocations and procurement failures forced a complete project redesign.
projects.detail: Approved at $1.3 billion in 2014, costs exploded to $3 billion by 2015, largely due to underestimated utility relocations and an unconventional contract that eliminated price competition. The project was halted and redesigned using design-build, cutting $700 million, but the final cost of $2.28 billion still far exceeded the original budget. Opened in 2022, eight years after the 2014 target.

projects.name: MARTA Rapid A-Line BRT (Atlanta)
projects.description: Atlanta's first BRT line more than doubled from $58M to $123M after crews discovered unmarked water lines, a forgotten underground parking garage, and buried 1920s streetcar tracks.
projects.detail: MARTA's Rapid A-Line BRT connecting downtown Atlanta to Summerhill was budgeted at $58 million. Construction crews discovered shallow unmarked water lines, a forgotten underground parking garage on Forsyth Street, and two sets of old trolley tracks requiring archaeological assessment from the State Historical Preservation Office. Costs pushed to $122.9 million and completion was delayed to fall 2026.

projects.name: Katy Freeway (I-10) Reconstruction
projects.description: 25-mile freeway widening required over $300M in utility relocations alone, with total costs jumping from $1.5B to $2.8B.
projects.detail: TxDOT's cost estimate grew from $1.504 billion to $2.8 billion at completion. Right-of-way acquisition, relocation assistance, and utility relocations totaled $599 million, with utility relocations alone exceeding $300 million. A state audit found TxDOT did not take necessary steps to estimate total project costs. The project made I-10 the widest freeway in the world at 26 lanes.

projects.name: Charlotte LYNX Blue Line Extension
projects.description: 11-mile light rail extension delayed 8 months after underground utility relocation threatened a full year setback; line truncated short of I-485 due to cost overruns.
projects.detail: The LYNX Blue Line Extension was budgeted at $1.16 billion. When the project manager started in 2014, he discovered utility relocation delays threatened to push the project back a year. CATS encountered difficulties relocating underground utilities. The extension opened March 16, 2018, eight months late. CATS ran out of money before reaching the planned I-485 terminus.

projects.name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel (Thimble Shoal)
projects.description: Tunnel boring machine struck a buried century-old ship anchor during construction, halting work for 10 months and delaying the $756M project by five years.
projects.detail: The Parallel Thimble Shoal Tunnel was approved in 2013 at $756 million with completion for 2023. During boring, the tunnel boring machine 'Chessie' struck a century-old ship anchor buried in the seafloor that was not found in preliminary surveys. The anchor halted tunneling for nearly ten months while crews repaired damaged equipment. Completion has slipped to 2028.

projects.name: Cross Lanes Road Widening
projects.description: Road widening stalled for months due to utility relocation disputes, with agencies and utility companies unable to coordinate pole ownership.
projects.detail: The $18.75 million WV 622 widening project began in August 2023 with a projected June 2025 completion. Construction paused in October 2024 when utility relocations took far longer than expected. Disputes arose over ownership of utility poles, and utilities supposed to be moved by May 2025 were not. The WVDOT acknowledged the delay was not the contractor's fault.

projects.name: Clay Road Reconstruction (Harris County)
projects.description: Road reconstruction delayed two years by gas pipeline relocations, as Energy Transfer and Kinder Morgan prioritized other regional projects.
projects.detail: Harris County's Clay Road reconstruction required relocation of natural gas pipelines owned by Energy Transfer and Kinder Morgan. The utility companies' regional project queues caused an estimated two-year delay. Utility relocation began in summer 2025, with road construction expected to start in late 2025 and take 18-24 months.
projects.budget: Multimillion-dollar county project — final cost TBD

projects.name: Cortez Bridge Utility Relocation
projects.description: Bridge replacement utility relocation grew from $7.2M to $8.8M, extending through 2026 and delaying the $143M bridge replacement start.
projects.detail: Manatee County's utility relocation ahead of the $143 million Cortez Bridge replacement required relocating 24-inch water mains and 20-inch force mains. The utility scope grew from $7.2 million to $8.8 million. Utility work extended through summer 2026, pushing the bridge construction bid date to March 2026.

projects.name: Oxbo Road Realignment (Roswell GA)
projects.description: Road realignment stalled for nearly two years due to Georgia Power utility pole relocation delays and lack of a utility relocation plan; cost soared from $7M to $18.4M.
projects.detail: The project soared from $7 million in 2016 to $18.4 million. An independent investigation found no project manager and no utility relocation plan. Georgia Power had issues acquiring easements for utility pole relocation, causing 'significant delay and rework.' Most roadwork stopped for nearly two years while Georgia Power relocated utility poles. The road was closed for three years before reopening in June 2023.

projects.name: Route 44 Relocation (Plymouth MA)
projects.description: Highway relocation cost $23M more than budgeted and took 2,200 extra days, with utility company delays accounting for 28% of all schedule extensions.
projects.detail: The Route 44 relocation was originally budgeted at $34 million but cost $57 million and took nearly 2,200 additional days beyond the original estimate. It was the second-highest cost overrun project in Massachusetts. Utility company relocation delays accounted for 28 percent of all schedule extensions in MassDOT projects. Officials noted utility companies do not prioritize state projects since they are not a revenue source.

projects.name: Fore River Bridge Replacement
projects.description: Bridge replacement topped Massachusetts cost overrun list at $87.9M vs $58M budget, with utility relocation issues contributing significantly to delays.
projects.detail: The Fore River Bridge on Route 3A linking Quincy and Weymouth was originally priced at $58 million but ballooned to $87.9 million, the highest cost overrun project in Massachusetts. Utility relocation issues, design flaws, weather, and environmental concerns all contributed. MassDOT acknowledged utility companies have been problematic because state projects are not a revenue source.

projects.name: I-490/IL 390 Tollway Interchange
projects.description: Contractor sued tollway for $29.4M after utility relocations and missing easements turned a 13-month bridge timeline into 777 days of delay.
projects.detail: The $534 million interchange project near O'Hare Airport faced massive delays when the Illinois Tollway failed to secure required easements and complete utility relocations before awarding contracts. A 13-month timeline to construct a Union Pacific Railroad bridge 'turned out to be wildly untrue' as Judlau Contracting waited 777 days before work could begin. A retaining wall project lost 514 days for similar reasons.

projects.name: West Hundred Road (Route 10) Widening
projects.description: Road widening ran 361 days past deadline with $1.44M in liquidated damages due to utility conflicts not shown in construction plans.
projects.detail: The $65.9 million Route 10 widening from four to eight lanes was granted permission in October 2019 with April 2022 completion. Contractor Branscome reported 361 days late due to utility conflicts not shown in plans and incorrect elevations. Branscome is seeking nearly $14 million in additional payment. The county assessed $1.44 million in liquidated damages.

projects.name: Energize Eastside Transmission Line
projects.description: 16-mile transmission line upgrade completed six years late, with permitting and coordination delays pushing costs up $52.4 million.
projects.detail: Puget Sound Energy's Energize Eastside project to upgrade transmission lines from Redmond to Renton was launched in 2013 but did not complete until December 2024. The utility needed the line by 2018 but six years of environmental studies, public hearings, and permitting conflicts pushed the timeline. Costs increased from $250 million to over $300 million.

projects.name: Rolling Road Widening (Springfield VA)
projects.description: Road widening delayed five years in the utility relocation phase alone, with utility pole relocations as the primary bottleneck.
projects.detail: VDOT's $51.6 million project to widen 1.4 miles of Rolling Road has experienced years of utility-driven delays. Phase I utility relocation was planned for Spring 2019 but was repeatedly pushed back. The project is now scheduled for completion in late 2027, roughly five years behind schedule.

projects.name: Google Fiber Louisville Microtrenching Failure
projects.description: Google Fiber's shallow nanotrenching destroyed road surfaces across neighborhoods, with cables popping out; Google abandoned the city and paid $3.84M in road repairs.
projects.detail: Google Fiber installed cables just two inches below street surfaces using epoxy instead of asphalt. Vehicle traffic ripped up the epoxy, exposing cables that created pedestrian hazards in Portland, Newburg, and Highlands neighborhoods. After only 16 months of service, Google abandoned Louisville in February 2019 and paid $3.84 million to repair roads plus $150,000 to the city's Digital Inclusion Fund.
projects.budget: $0 city cost → $3.84M settlement for road repairs

projects.name: Dauphin County Road UGI Dig-Up
projects.description: PennDOT completed repaving Chambers Hill Road only for UGI gas company and Veolia water company to tear it up weeks later.
projects.detail: In August 2022, just weeks after PennDOT finished repaving Chambers Hill Road between 80th and 82nd streets, UGI gas company and Veolia water company began ripping up the fresh pavement to move and upgrade pipes. PennDOT stated it had told UGI to do the work before paving. UGI claimed PennDOT approved its permit. UGI agreed to cover restoration costs.
projects.timeline: Summer 2022 paving → Weeks later UGI excavation → October 2022 restoration

projects.name: Gigapower/AT&T Mesa Fiber Infrastructure Damage
projects.description: AT&T's Gigapower fiber contractors caused at least 40 underground utility hits totaling $135,000 in damage in just 18 months, while microtrenching deteriorated road surfaces.
projects.detail: Gigapower began work in Mesa less than three weeks after being licensed in July 2024 and immediately hit a water main. Over 18 months, contractors caused at least 40 underground utility hits to gas, water, and sewer lines. Road surfaces deteriorated weeks after microtrenching, with cracks developing and fill material failing. The HOA President at Superstition Springs reported contractors hit the community gas line three times.
projects.timeline: July 2024 licensing → August 2024 first water hit → December 2024 CWA report

projects.name: Gigapower/AT&T Chandler Fiber Shutdowns
projects.description: Gigapower's fiber deployment experienced five city-ordered work shutdowns in one year due to safety concerns, with multiple underground utility hits.
projects.detail: Between December 2023 and March 2025, Gigapower contractors hit water mains, sewer lines, and electrical infrastructure multiple times in Chandler. The city ordered five work stoppages due to public safety and road restoration issues. Gigapower used 28 different subcontractors, at least two not registered in Arizona. Communication with inspectors was 'combative and dismissive.' Prime contractor Tilson was dismissed in April 2025.
projects.timeline: June 2023 → Five shutdowns through February 2025 → April 2025 contractor dismissed

projects.name: Durham NC AT&T Fiber Permit Freeze
projects.description: Durham received over 200 complaints about AT&T fiber road and property damage, prompting the city to freeze all AT&T permits until complaints were resolved.
projects.detail: AT&T's fiber installation generated over 200 complaints related to property not restored to satisfaction, including 40 asphalt damage complaints. Durham refused to issue additional permits and required AT&T to fix all outstanding complaints before resuming. Chapel Hill received over 90 similar complaints. Damages included broken driveways, cut utility lines, and holes left in yards.

projects.name: Spokane Cheney Road Freshly Repaved Dig-Up
projects.description: Construction crews dug up freshly repaved Cheney-Spokane Road to replace a water main pipe, acknowledged by the city as appearing out of order to residents.
projects.detail: In September 2024, crews dug up the freshly repaved Cheney-Spokane Road to install a 30-inch water transmission main as part of a $9.9 million infrastructure project. The city acknowledged this seemed out of order but stated the water main replacement was planned and that leaving the entire street unpaved during the multi-phase water project would have been worse. The road was finally repaved in October 2024.
projects.timeline: April 2024 → September 2024 freshly paved road dug up → October 2024 final repaving

projects.name: NYC Protected Street Permit Failures
projects.description: State Comptroller audit found NYC DOT failed to inspect 14% of 299,933 street opening permits and did not ensure compliance with protected street requirements.
projects.detail: The 2022 New York State Comptroller audit found that 41,761 of 299,933 street opening permits (14%) that should have been inspected were not. Of 73 reinspections reviewed, none had proper documentation, and 11% still showed unresolved problems. Protected streets — those resurfaced within the past 5 years — were supposed to be off-limits except for emergencies, but compliance failures persisted.
projects.budget: $60M annual resurfacing → $65M accounting for premature degradation

projects.name: Troy Rochester Road Widening Utility Relocation Delays
projects.description: Troy's Rochester Road widening was slowed by utility relocations, including DTE pole moves that exposed an unknown city-owned fiber line requiring an emergency relocation.
projects.detail: Troy is widening Rochester Road with about $22 million in federal/MDOT funds and about $5.6 million in city funds. A city-owned fiber cable serving the Public Works building had been mounted on five DTE-owned poles since 1999, and those poles were being relocated for the widening. The team handling utility relocation was not initially aware of the fiber on those poles, and it took time to determine the city owned it. In July 2026 the council approved an emergency relocation costing about $15,300, plus up to $12,000 for possible underground conduit replacement, scheduled to avoid delaying road work.
projects.timeline: Fall 2025 start -> lanes open end of 2026 -> restoration 2027

projects.name: Ann Arbor East Huron River Drive Retaining Wall Delay (DTE Conflicts)
projects.description: Ann Arbor's $712,000 East Huron River Drive retaining wall replacement stalled because of unforeseen conflicts with DTE Energy's overhead electrical facilities, leaving the road closed.
projects.detail: In March 2026 Ann Arbor approved a $712,000 contract to replace the East Huron River Drive retaining wall between Chalmers Drive and Riverside Drive and reconstruct the roadway. The city later reported the project was delayed by unforeseen utility conflicts with DTE Energy's overhead electrical facilities, which proved more complex than anticipated. Because the guardrail, retaining wall and slope were deemed unsafe, the road remained closed. The city said work would restart once DTE completed its utility work.
projects.timeline: Contract approved Mar 2026 -> road closed from late May 2026; restart pending DTE work

projects.name: Novi Road Reconstruction Stalled Awaiting DTE Pole Relocation
projects.description: The Road Commission for Oakland County's Novi Road project between Nine and Ten Mile stalled in its third phase while waiting for DTE to move utility poles, frustrating residents.
projects.detail: RCOC's Novi Road project between Nine Mile and Ten Mile began in March 2023. By August, residents complained of inconsistent progress. The road commission said it was waiting for DTE to move its utility poles, work it knew had to be done the previous year, and noted state law does not let it fine utilities for inaction. DTE was replacing poles as part of grid upgrades, which required each utility to transfer its equipment before the old pole could be removed. Completion was scheduled for mid-November 2023.

projects.name: Webster Township N. Territorial Road Repeat DTE Gas Line Strikes
projects.description: Construction crews at the N. Territorial and Webster Church Road project area struck 2-inch DTE/MichCon gas lines twice in one week, closing the road and evacuating a party store.
projects.detail: On April 18, 2024, construction crews working in the N. Territorial and Webster Church project area in Webster Township struck a 2-inch, 60 psi natural gas line about 150 feet west of the intersection. On April 25 the crew hit another 2-inch line. DTE/MichCon responded, N. Territorial Road was closed between east of Scully Road and Lori Lane until repairs were made, and CJ's party store was closed and evacuated as a precaution. No injuries were reported.
projects.timeline: Strikes April 18 and April 25, 2024; road reopened next morning

projects.name: Traverse City Veterans Drive Reconstruction DTE Gas Main Strike
projects.description: An excavator on Traverse City's Veterans Drive reconstruction hit a marked 3-inch DTE gas main, closing 14th Street for hours and shutting two businesses.
projects.detail: Around 11 a.m. on July 29, 2024, an excavator working on the Veterans Drive reconstruction project hit a 3-inch gas main. Police and firefighters closed 14th Street and detoured traffic. Team One Credit Union and Redmond Automotive closed after the leak, and two nearby businesses had gas service interrupted during repairs. DTE said the line had been marked before the incident. The road was cleared to reopen around 4 p.m.

projects.name: Traverse City Water Main Contractor DTE Gas Line Strike (Winding Trail)
projects.description: An excavation contractor working on a subdivision water main hit a DTE gas line with an excavator bucket near South Winding Trail and M-72, forcing about 10 homes to evacuate.
projects.detail: Just after 10 a.m. on September 14, 2022, an excavation contractor working on the water main in a subdivision at South Winding Trail and M-72 near Traverse City hit a gas line with an excavator bucket. Around 10 homes were evacuated while DTE repaired the leak. Crews cleared the area just before noon.

projects.name: Belle Isle Gas Line Strike During DTE Grid Conversion
projects.description: A contractor preparing to feed a DTE electric line under the Detroit River to Belle Isle struck a gas line, cutting natural gas service to the island park's buildings.
projects.detail: In late November 2018 DTE was converting Belle Isle buildings from Detroit Public Lighting Department infrastructure to a new DTE-operated grid. A contractor preparing to feed an electric line under the Detroit River struck a gas line, and buildings on the island lost natural gas service. The gas flow was shut off and no one was injured. DTE worked with park facilities on temporary heating while gas service was restored.

projects.name: Grosse Pointe Woods Wedgewood Gas Line Strike
projects.description: A construction crew struck a major gas line on Wedgewood Street, forcing home evacuations and a lockdown at Grosse Pointe North High School.
projects.detail: Late in the morning of May 9, 2017, a construction crew struck a major gas line on Wedgewood Street near Vernier Road and Morningside Drive in Grosse Pointe Woods. Homes from Wedgewood to the city's east limits were evacuated and Grosse Pointe North High School was locked down. The gas was shut off and residents returned home; DTE Energy expected repairs to be finished around 5 p.m.

projects.name: Grosse Pointe Farms Moran Road Third-Party Gas Strike
projects.description: A third-party contractor digging near 126 Moran Road struck a DTE gas line, prompting evacuations in Grosse Pointe Farms.
projects.detail: On June 16, 2026, a third-party contractor digging near 126 Moran Road in Grosse Pointe Farms struck a gas line, and residents in the area were evacuated. DTE crews stopped the leak and residents were allowed to return. DTE reminded excavators to call MISS DIG 811 before digging.

projects.name: Lake Orion Baldwin Road Repaving Cut by Consumers Gas Work
projects.description: Consumers Energy dug up a stretch of Baldwin Road near Morgan within a month of the Road Commission for Oakland County repaving it, to work on aging gas lines.
projects.detail: The Road Commission for Oakland County added new asphalt to Baldwin Road near Morgan in the Lake Orion area, and shortly afterward Consumers Energy began digging it up to work on aging underground gas lines. Drivers and businesses complained of backups, and the road commission called the situation frustrating. A road commission spokesperson said the road may be weaker long term where it was torn up and repaired. Consumers Energy is paying for restoration.
projects.timeline: Repaved summer 2026 -> dug up within about a month (Aug 2026)

projects.name: Burton Consumers Gas Main Work Damaging Repaved Roads
projects.description: Burton council members said Consumers Energy gas-main replacement work, with trenching and temporary patches, damaged recently repaved corridors including Center and Bristol roads.
projects.detail: At a May 5, 2025 meeting, Burton City Council members pressed Consumers Energy over damage from gas-main replacement work on Center Road, Bristol Road and other corridors, including directional drilling and temporary patches. One council member referenced about $3.4 million in recent paving between Lippincott and Atherton. A council member said the work had destroyed the road in places. City staff said they meet regularly with Consumers but have limited control over the utility's timing and methods.

projects.name: Kalamazoo South Westnedge City Crew Gas Line Strike
projects.description: A City of Kalamazoo construction crew working on Westnedge Avenue hit a Consumers Energy gas line, closing South Westnedge from Pioneer Street to Crosstown Parkway overnight.
projects.detail: Around 10 a.m. on a Wednesday in early September 2026, a City of Kalamazoo construction crew working on Westnedge Avenue hit a gas line, causing a large natural gas leak. South Westnedge was closed from Pioneer Street to west Crosstown Parkway. Consumers Energy crews shut off the gas and worked through the night, with repairs expected Thursday afternoon. No customers lost gas service.
projects.timeline: September 2026; closed overnight into next afternoon

projects.name: Lansing Two-Way Street Conversions Delayed by Utility Relocations
projects.description: Lansing's downtown one-way to two-way street conversions slipped from November 2021 to May 2022 after utility relocations took several months longer than expected.
projects.detail: Lansing planned to finish converting several downtown streets from one-way to two-way traffic in November 2021. The city said utility relocations for the project took several months longer than anticipated. Traffic signal work was also slowed by delivery delays and staffing issues, and pavement markings could not be applied in cold, wet weather. Completion was postponed to May 2022.

projects.name: Novi Road Construction Gas Main Strike near I-96
projects.description: A construction crew in a major road construction zone near I-96 hit a Consumers Energy plastic gas main at Novi Road and Main Street, evacuating businesses and cutting gas to about 165 customers.
projects.detail: On June 14, 2011, a construction crew hit a gas line near Novi Road and Main Street, in a major road construction area not far from I-96. About six businesses were evacuated and the intersection was closed. Consumers Energy said about 165 customers, mostly residential and a nearby apartment complex, would lose gas service during repairs.

projects.name: Novi West Oaks Gordon Food Service Site Gas Main Strike
projects.description: A grading and paving contractor at a future Gordon Food Service store hit a 4-inch Consumers Energy gas main, evacuating Kohl's and other West Oaks Plaza stores.
projects.detail: On September 4, 2013, a contractor doing grading and paving for a future Gordon Food Service store at West Oaks Plaza near 12 Mile and Novi Road hit a four-inch gas main. Kohl's and several smaller stores were evacuated as gas vented, and firefighters and Consumers Energy crews shut off the gas. All stores reopened by 4:30 p.m. with no injuries.

projects.name: Hoboken Water Emergency from PSE&G Contractor Main Strike
projects.description: A PSE&G contractor doing gas line work struck an unmarked water main in Hoboken, leaving about 58,000 residents without water and forcing a hospital evacuation.
projects.detail: Around noon on Monday, February 27, 2023, a PSE&G contractor, J. Fletcher Creamer & Son, struck a water main in Hoboken while working on an unrelated gas line project. According to NBC New York, the water main was unmarked. The break left about 58,000 Hoboken residents without water, forced a hospital evacuation, and service was mostly restored overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, with a boil water advisory remaining afterward. Mayor Ravi Bhalla announced the city's intent to sue PSE&G and the contractor. In July 2023 the city announced a settlement in which J. Fletcher Creamer and Veolia provided nearly $1 million in funding and services; PSE&G was part of the settlement but provided no funds.
projects.timeline: Feb 27, 2023 strike → service mostly restored ~Mar 1, 2023 → settlement July 2023

projects.name: Wayne Lions Head Lake Roads Left Damaged by PSE&G Gas Main Work
projects.description: After PSE&G gas main replacement left two dozen roads around Lions Head Lake in poor shape, Wayne spent months pressing PSE&G to pay for a $2.2M repaving.
projects.detail: Wayne officials said PSE&G crews left roads around Lions Head Lake in terrible shape when they replaced gas mains there. Mayor Christopher Vergano said the township met multiple times with PSE&G executives to resolve the dispute, which was at an impasse for weeks. Two dozen roads in the lakefront neighborhood were ultimately paved, along with David Scott Drive and Douglas Way, which were milled and paved by a PSE&G contractor. The full paving cost was $2.2 million; PSE&G covered two-thirds, leaving the township to pay $733,000.
projects.timeline: Dispute over months → roads paved by Sept 2024

projects.name: Bergenfield Apartment Explosion During Oil Tank Excavation (NTSB)
projects.description: An excavation to remove a buried oil tank next to a Bergenfield apartment building undermined a PSE&G gas service line, causing an explosion that killed three people.
projects.detail: JP Management hired American Tank Service Company to remove a buried oil tank under the parking lot at 30 Elm Street in Bergenfield; PSE&G marked the gas service line before work began. The tank turned out to be 5,000 gallons rather than 2,000, requiring a trench about 24 feet long, and the trench was not shored. On December 13, 2005, the soil collapsed, the service line separated at a threaded tee, and gas migrated into the building, which exploded at 9:26 a.m., killing three residents and injuring five people. The NTSB found the probable cause was the contractor's failure to protect the service line, with PSE&G's ineffective oversight of the excavation and inability to promptly shut off gas contributing. The NJ Board of Public Utilities cited PSE&G for three probable violations; property damage was $863,300.
projects.timeline: Excavation Dec 12, 2005 → explosion Dec 13, 2005 → NTSB brief adopted May 1, 2007

projects.name: Montclair Bloomfield Avenue Trench Hits Mismarked PSE&G Gas Main
projects.description: A construction crew digging a trench at Bloomfield Avenue and South Park Street hit a gas main that fire officials said was not marked out properly, displacing about 100 people.
projects.detail: On April 30, 2012, a construction crew digging a trench on Bloomfield Avenue and South Park Street in Montclair struck a gas main. Fire Captain Thomas Diveny said the line was not marked out properly. PSE&G crews said the break was in a six-inch plastic gas line. About 100 people were evacuated as a precaution and the all-clear was issued just before 2 p.m.

projects.name: Summit Prospect Street Culvert Repair Ruptures PSE&G Gas Main
projects.description: A contractor on a Prospect Street culvert repair in Summit dropped a concrete slab on a PSE&G gas main, rupturing it and closing the street.
projects.detail: Jogi Construction of Edison was hired for a culvert repair on Prospect Street in Summit that began around February 27, 2012. On March 28, 2012, a contractor dropped a concrete slab on a gas main, rupturing it, according to PSE&G. Police set up road blocks along Prospect Street from Linden Place to Springfield Avenue, and some residents were expected to be without gas until PSE&G finished repairs.

projects.name: Berkeley Heights Glenside Road Paving Delayed by PSE&G Gas Main Work
projects.description: An unexpected extension of PSE&G gas main work on Glenside Road delayed Berkeley Heights' planned repaving of the road.
projects.detail: Berkeley Heights gave utilities a list of recently paved roads, placing a moratorium on work on those streets, and a list of roads to be paved within the next year. PSE&G gas main work on Glenside Road was expected to be completed by mid-September, after which trenches needed weeks to settle before PSE&G could pave the portions it dug up. The township said the unexpected extension of utility work in the area had delayed its own paving of the road and that it was in discussions with PSE&G about how to proceed.

projects.name: Route 18 East Brunswick Rehabilitation Unmapped Utilities
projects.description: NJDOT's $86.1M Route 18 rehabilitation in East Brunswick had to resolve unmapped utility lines and an abandoned culvert during construction while relocating PSE&G-connected gas mains.
projects.detail: NJDOT's $86.1 million project rehabilitates a 4.14-mile stretch of Route 18 in East Brunswick; it broke ground in January 2023 with substantial completion expected in late 2027. Challenges during construction included unmapped utility lines, drainage and other underground features that had to be resolved with additional full-depth pavement reconstruction. An abandoned large underground culvert found during grading required geotechnical solutions, and a deteriorated pipe arch required a redesign approved by NJDEP as a major technical modification. Gas mains were being relocated to make room for new drainage and water systems, with PSE&G assisting on gas main tie-ins.

projects.name: East Brunswick Nenninger Lane Developer Breaks Water and Sewer Mains
projects.description: A contractor installing a sewer line for a new house broke East Brunswick's water and sewer mains on Nenninger Lane, causing an estimated $103,295 in repairs.
projects.detail: A contractor installing a sewer line for a new house at 10 Nenninger Lane in East Brunswick broke both the township's water and sewer mains. The street lost water and fire protection. Repairs were estimated at $103,294.59, and the sewer main was still damaged at the time of reporting. A township certification blamed 'extremely poor practice' by the contractor, and the township sought repayment from the contractor, its insurer or the property owner, with a lien possible if unpaid.

projects.name: Lower Broadway Phase 1 Timeline Stretched for CPS/SAWS Work (San Antonio)
projects.description: The first phase of San Antonio's $43M Broadway bond project was pushed from 2021 into 2023 so the street work could be aligned with CPS Energy and SAWS utility work.
projects.detail: The 2.2-mile Broadway Street redevelopment is a $43 million 2017 bond project, with the entire corridor estimated for completion by the end of 2024. The first phase (East Houston Street to I-35) was originally slated for completion in 2021, but the City worked with local utilities to align the project with planned maintenance along Broadway, stretching that phase into 2023. An assistant city engineer said the coordination was meant to avoid someone cutting a trench in the new street two years after it was built, referring to work being done on the street by CPS Energy and SAWS.

projects.name: Downtown Underground Cable Strike at El Paso & Santa Rosa (San Antonio)
projects.description: A private construction crew damaged a CPS Energy underground cable near El Paso and Santa Rosa streets, knocking out power to more than 300 downtown customers.
projects.detail: On November 10, 2021, a private construction company working near El Paso and Santa Rosa streets in downtown San Antonio damaged an underground cable, according to CPS Energy. The outage affected more than 300 CPS Energy customers in the area. CPS Energy crews responded that afternoon and expected restoration to take four to five hours; power was later restored. CPS called it an isolated incident.

projects.name: Two Gas Main Strikes in One Day, US 281 & Loop 1604 (San Antonio)
projects.description: Construction crews hit two separate 4-inch CPS Energy natural gas mains on San Antonio's Far North Side on the same day in November 2017.
projects.detail: On November 1, 2017, a construction crew digging near the US 281 access road by Sonterra struck a four-inch natural gas line. Just after noon, a second 4-inch gas main was hit near Loop 1604 and Blanco Road by the Vineyard Shopping Center, where SAPD provided traffic control while crews shut off the main. A CPS Energy spokesperson called two strikes in the same area on one day a rarity and stressed that contractors are required by law to have lines located before digging. CPS Energy hosted a free digging and trenching safety presentation for excavators the next day.

projects.name: Stone Oak Parkway Gas Main Rupture (San Antonio)
projects.description: A construction crew ruptured a natural gas main on Stone Oak Parkway, closing the road in both directions while hazmat and CPS Energy crews responded.
projects.detail: On the morning of November 1, 2022, a construction crew ruptured a natural gas main on Stone Oak Parkway near Knight's Cross on San Antonio's North Side. Stone Oak Parkway was closed in both directions from Knight's Cross to Arrow Hill while hazmat crews and CPS Energy workers stopped the leak and monitored air quality. No homes or businesses were evacuated, and the road reopened at about 12:30 p.m.

projects.name: I-10 Leon Springs Frontage Roads: CPS Gas and AT&T Conflicts (San Antonio)
projects.description: TxDOT's I-10 Leon Springs frontage-road conversion was held up by an AT&T/Qwest line conflict and by CPS Energy gas-line relocation conflicts.
projects.detail: TxDOT's I-10 Leon Springs project converted frontage roads between Dominion Drive and Boerne Stage Road, with Texas Sterling Construction as contractor and a scheduled finish of mid-2016. In May 2015 TxDOT reported a major utility conflict at the Boerne Stage Road intersection with an AT&T/Qwest line, with the contractor working around the area until the line could be relocated. Gas lines were being relocated across the job, but conflicts with CPS Energy had to be worked out before some of them could be moved, including many that had been planned to move the previous week.

projects.name: FM 1560 (Hausman Rd) Gas Line & Sewer Conflicts Force Plan Changes (San Antonio)
projects.description: Gas line and sewer elevation conflicts at Hausman and Bandera forced TxDOT to change plans and keep a key right-turn lane closed about two months longer.
projects.detail: TxDOT's FM 1560 (Hausman Road) expansion from Loop 1604 to SH 16 (Bandera Road) required major gas, water, sewer, electric and fiber utility work before roadway construction, with a first utility phase of about 18 months and completion estimated for early 2023. In March 2019 TxDOT said the utility challenge was forcing significant changes to the original plans: the gas line under the Hausman–Bandera intersection proved difficult, and the contractor hit elevation conflicts at sanitary sewer connections under the right-turn lane. That forced a temporary halt and a slope redesign, and the turn-lane reopening slipped to May 20, about two more months. TxDOT then had the contractor do all permanent utility work under the lane at once instead of over three years.
projects.timeline: Utility phase ~18 months; project completion estimated early 2023

projects.name: North St. Mary's Street ('The Strip') Sewer & Utility Delays (San Antonio)
projects.description: The St. Mary's Strip bond reconstruction ran months late, blamed partly on unforeseen soil and utility challenges and about 250 feet of sewer pipe laid at the wrong elevation.
projects.detail: Reconstruction of North St. Mary's Street (the 'St. Mary's Strip') began in 2021. In January 2023 officials attributed the delays to wet weather, unforeseen challenges with the soil and utilities, and contractor errors. A SpawGlass representative said about 250 feet of sewer pipe had been installed at the wrong elevation before the responsible contractor was removed. The City said roadways would be substantially complete by March 2023, with sidewalks, landscaping and lighting following in summer, and that it would assess $1,300 per day in liquidated damages for missed deadlines.
projects.timeline: 2021 start → roadway March 2023, finishing work summer 2023 (per Jan 2023 update)

projects.name: North New Braunfels Avenue Phase 1 Utility Delays (San Antonio)
projects.description: The East Side North New Braunfels Avenue bond project slipped from May to July 2023, first because of utility issues related to old pipes.
projects.detail: Construction on North New Braunfels Avenue between Burleson Street and East Houston Street on San Antonio's East Side began in November 2021. City officials cited utility issues, tight working conditions with two-way traffic, and weather as reasons for delays. The Public Works director said the delays were at first due to utility issues related to old pipes. Completion, previously expected in May 2023, was pushed to July 2023, and small business owners along the corridor said the work hurt them.

projects.name: FM 1103 Widening Halted ~2 Years by Utility Conflicts (Cibolo)
projects.description: TxDOT's FM 1103 widening between I-35 and Rodeo Way in Cibolo stalled for about two years over utility conflicts, pushing completion from late 2025/early 2026 to 2029.
projects.detail: TxDOT is widening FM 1103 in Cibolo from two lanes to four with a center turn lane, bike lanes and sidewalks between Interstate 35 and Rodeo Way. TxDOT originally posted that construction would finish by late 2025 or early 2026. Officials said the delay was caused by utility conflicts: above-ground and underground utility lines were in the way, and resolving the issue took about two years. As of September 2026 the project is expected to finish in 2029.

projects.name: Fiber Buildout Water Line Breaks (Google Fiber/AT&T, San Antonio)
projects.description: Subcontractors installing fiber for Google and AT&T broke SAWS water lines three times in 2015–2016, costing SAWS $28,512 in repairs.
projects.detail: As Google Fiber and AT&T built fiber networks in San Antonio, open-records documents showed their subcontractors broke SAWS water lines. In June 2016 crews installing Google Fiber on Haskin Drive broke a water line, which SAWS paid $3,452 to fix. A Google subcontractor caused a $16,022 break in March 2016, and an AT&T subcontractor caused a $9,038 break in January 2015. The City responded by requiring fiber builders to give 30 days' notice, post message boards and hang door notices before work.

projects.name: FM 1101 Project Stalled 18+ Months by Utility Conflicts (New Braunfels)
projects.description: TxDOT's FM 1101 project in New Braunfels waited more than a year and a half on utility conflicts, leaving its 2014 bid prices out of date.
projects.detail: TxDOT reported in May 2016 that most of the utility conflicts that had kept it from doing the FM 1101 work were finally out of the way, after it had waited more than a year and a half. The contractor, Hunter Industries, had bid the project in 2014 at 2014 prices. Two years later, TxDOT and the contractor were negotiating an equitable middle ground on pricing before work could get going.

projects.name: UTSA Boulevard Start Delayed by Utility Conflicts (San Antonio)
projects.delayAbs: Start moved from April to June 22, 2015
projects.description: Utility conflicts kept TxDOT's UTSA Boulevard project from starting in April 2015 as planned; work began June 22.
projects.detail: TxDOT said in June 2015 that utility conflicts had kept it from starting the UTSA Boulevard project in April, when it had wanted to start. After receiving notice to proceed, work was set to begin June 22, 2015 on the eastbound side first. The overall project was expected to take two full years.
projects.timeline: April 2015 planned start → June 22, 2015 actual; ~2-year duration

projects.name: FM 306 Gas Line Rupture During AT&T Relocation (New Braunfels)
projects.description: AT&T contractors relocating communication lines for TxDOT's FM 306 expansion ruptured a CenterPoint Energy gas line, closing FM 306 completely.
projects.detail: In August 2013, crews contracted by AT&T were digging to move communication lines for TxDOT's FM 306 expansion project in New Braunfels when they ruptured a CenterPoint Energy gas line. The line, about 20 to 30 feet from the roadway near the Wingate Hotel, blew gas across the road, and police and fire closed FM 306 entirely between I-35 and Goodwin Lane. CenterPoint crews clamped the line and the road reopened a little after 1 p.m.

projects.name: I-35 Windcrest–SAMMC Project Delays Incl. Utility Conflicts (San Antonio)
projects.description: TxDOT's I-35 auxiliary-lane project between Windcrest and SAMMC, set to finish near the end of 2016, ran into 2017 amid plan discrepancies, contractor resource issues and utility conflicts.
projects.detail: TxDOT's I-35 project between Windcrest and SAMMC added an auxiliary lane in each direction and adjusted ramps. It began in 2013 and was initially set to wrap up near the end of 2016, but carried into 2017. TxDOT said a slew of issues had plagued the project, ranging from discrepancies in the plan sheets to resource allocation by contractor Lane Construction to utility conflicts. TxDOT said it would review responsibility for the delays after completion and assess liquidated damages as appropriate.

projects.name: Eustis Fiber Drilling Gas Strike and Fatal Explosion
projects.description: A horizontal directional drill installing fiber-optic infrastructure struck a Peoples Gas line in downtown Eustis, and a nearby building exploded about 90 minutes later, killing its owner.
projects.detail: On Dec. 4, 2025, a worker for Mendoza Conduit Installers struck a natural gas line while running a horizontal directional drill owned by FiberPro Network Services for a fiber-optic build near South Eustis Street. Peoples Gas squeezed off the damaged line at about 10:48 a.m., and the building at 101 S. Eustis St. exploded about nine minutes later. Business owner Wendy Davis was badly burned and died two days later. A wrongful-death suit filed in September 2026 names Peoples Gas, fiber provider Wire 3 LLC, design firm Alson Services, FiberPro and Mendoza. It alleges the line was not properly marked before drilling began and that the drill operator was unlicensed. These are allegations in the lawsuit, not findings.
projects.timeline: Dec 4, 2025 strike and explosion; lawsuit filed Sept 2026

projects.name: Eustis Fiber Construction Gas Line Strike (August 2026)
projects.description: A third-party fiber contractor's drilling equipment hit a TECO Peoples Gas pipeline in Eustis, forcing evacuations less than half a mile from the December 2025 fatal explosion site.
projects.detail: On Aug. 11, 2026, a contractor for a company installing a fiber line struck a natural gas pipeline with drilling equipment near Key Street and Center Street in Eustis. Nearby residents were evacuated and parts of South Center Street and Key Avenue were closed for repairs. TECO Peoples Gas crews repaired the leak, and the evacuation order was lifted the same day. Officials reminded contractors that Florida law requires a Sunshine 811 call before digging.

projects.name: Tampa Westshore Blvd / El Prado Construction Gas Strike
projects.description: Construction workers hit a TECO natural gas line at South Westshore Boulevard and West El Prado, and police diverted traffic for a block around the leak.
projects.detail: On Monday, May 11, 2026, construction workers struck a TECO natural gas line at the intersection of South Westshore Boulevard and West El Prado in Tampa. Tampa Police diverted traffic in a one-block radius while crews repaired the leak, and Tampa Fire Rescue supervised for safety. The source does not name the construction project or say how long repairs took.

projects.name: Tampa N. 30th Street 8-Inch Gas Line Rupture
projects.description: Third-party construction equipment damaged an 8-inch TECO natural gas line at N. 30th Street and Bougainvillea Avenue, leading to a shelter-in-place order and closure of a county tax office.
projects.detail: In November 2024, TECO reported that an 8-inch natural gas pipeline at N. 30th Street and Bougainvillea Avenue in Tampa was damaged by third-party construction equipment. The City issued a shelter-in-place order, later rescinded, and the intersection was closed to vehicles and pedestrians. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector's North Tampa office closed for the day and reopened Wednesday, Nov. 20. TECO said the repair could take several hours.

projects.name: Orlando West Michigan Street TECO Gas Main Strike
projects.description: A construction crew hit one of TECO's main natural gas lines on West Michigan Street in Orlando, and the evacuation zone was widened to about 1,000 feet.
projects.detail: In August 2019, the Orlando Fire Department said a construction crew hit one of TECO's main natural gas lines on West Michigan Street, between South Division Avenue and I-4. Homes and businesses downwind were evacuated, about 15 in all. Firefighters widened the evacuation zone to about 1,000 feet once they found they could not control the leak themselves and called in TECO. TECO crews worked into the evening and restored service door to door the next day.

projects.name: Jacksonville San Marco Kings Avenue Gas Line Strike
projects.description: A third-party contractor damaged a 2-inch Peoples Gas pipeline near Kings Avenue in San Marco, forcing businesses to evacuate and leaving some customers without gas overnight.
projects.detail: On July 7, 2026, a third-party contractor damaged a 2-inch pipeline near Kings Avenue in Jacksonville's San Marco neighborhood. Businesses on the 1200 block of Kings Avenue near Naugle Way were evacuated, including SouthState Bank. No injuries were reported. Four customers were still without service that night, and Peoples Gas crews stopped initial repairs for the night and resumed restoration the next day.

projects.name: Marco Island LCEC Conduit Drilling Peoples Gas Strike
projects.description: A Lee County Electric Cooperative contractor drilling for new electrical conduit breached a 6-inch Peoples Gas line on Marco Island, which led to evacuations and a closed block of road for two days.
projects.detail: Around 12:30 p.m. on Jan. 7, 2025, a contractor for Lee County Electric Cooperative (LCEC) drilling for new electrical conduit breached a 6-inch gas line owned by TECO Energy's Peoples Gas. The leak was under Windward and Bald Eagle drives, and Walker's Marine and First Foundation Bank were evacuated. About a block stayed closed the next day while Peoples Gas finished repairs. A spokesperson said the contractor hit one of two TECO lines and that 'they weren't expecting it to be two lines.'

projects.name: I-4 Ultimate Altamonte Springs TECO Gas Line Strike
projects.description: An I-4 Ultimate contractor hit a 6-inch TECO steel gas pipe about 24 feet underground near the Altamonte Springs exit, stopping rush-hour traffic for hours.
projects.detail: In June 2018, a contractor on FDOT's I-4 Ultimate Project hit a 6-inch steel natural gas pipe near the Altamonte Springs exit, about 24 feet below ground. The strike brought traffic to a standstill for hours during rush hour. TECO said the gas lines had been marked correctly. The project contractor, SGL, did not respond to News 6's requests for comment.

projects.name: Lakeland East Palm Drive 4-Inch Gas Line Strike
projects.description: Construction crews struck a 4-inch TECO gas line near East Palm Drive in Lakeland, and residents across several streets were evacuated to a church.
projects.detail: On June 14, 2017, construction crews working near East Palm Drive in Lakeland struck a 4-inch gas line. A resident reported a strong smell of gas around 10:30 a.m. Residents near South Florida Avenue at East Beacon Road, East Palm Drive, Lake Hollingsworth Drive and nearby roads were evacuated to First Presbyterian Church. TECO Gas crews made the repairs, which were expected to take several hours.

projects.name: Lakeland Five Points Roundabout Utility Conflicts
projects.description: Lines from Lumen, TECO Energy and Frontier turned up inside Lakeland's Five Points roundabout work zone, even though all three companies had signed 'no conflict' letters, adding $151,429 in utility-conflict costs.
projects.detail: Construction on Lakeland's Five Points roundabout began Oct. 23, 2023, under a $2,207,556 contract. Crews found Lumen, TECO Energy and Frontier Communications facilities in the construction zone, even though all three companies had reviewed the plans and signed 'no conflict' letters. Among the finds were a 6-inch Lumen steel pipe carrying long-haul service and Frontier infrastructure dating to 1952. A $179,444 change order included $151,429 for the utility conflicts and raised the total to about $2,387,000, an 8% increase. The city said it would seek reimbursement from the utility owners, with Lumen's share estimated at $132,939. Despite the conflicts, the project was expected to finish about three months early.
projects.timeline: Oct 2023 start → spring 2024 (about 3 months ahead of schedule)

projects.name: Punta Gorda US 41 Gas Line Cut (St. Patrick's Day)
projects.description: A contractor cut a 4-inch TECO gas line under U.S. 41 near the Barron Collier Bridge, shutting off gas to about 85 customers in downtown Punta Gorda on St. Patrick's Day.
projects.detail: On St. Patrick's Day, March 17, 2026, a company TECO did not name cut a 4-inch natural gas line under Tamiami Trail (U.S. 41 north) near the Barron Collier Bridge. About 85 customers lost service, from Wood Street east to Fishermen's Village and south on U.S. 41. Downtown restaurants closed or changed how they operated on one of their busiest days. TECO restored gas business by business from 4 p.m. Tuesday until 10:30 a.m. Wednesday, and nine customers were still unrestored by 5 p.m. Wednesday.

projects.name: Tampa Tippin Water Plant 36-Inch Transmission Main Strike
projects.description: A third-party contractor hit a 36-inch transmission main leaving Tampa's David L. Tippin Water Treatment Facility, losing 12 million gallons and triggering a citywide boil-water notice.
projects.detail: At 3:24 p.m. on Dec. 7, 2020, a third-party contractor hit a 36-inch pressurized transmission main coming from the City of Tampa's David L. Tippin Water Treatment Facility. The main was 36-inch cast iron installed in 1941, and the damage cost 12 million gallons of water. Crews isolated the main and restored pressure by 6:06 p.m., and the pipe was replaced late the next evening. A precautionary boil-water notice covered all customers the city serves, including parts of unincorporated Hillsborough County. It was rescinded on Dec. 10 after testing.

projects.name: Citrus Park 24-Inch Water Main Strike (NW Hillsborough)
projects.description: A contractor modifying Hillsborough County's water distribution system near the Fawn Ridge Water Treatment Plant damaged a 24-inch main, which led to an outage and a boil-water notice across northwest Hillsborough.
projects.detail: On Dec. 15, 2020, a contractor modifying the existing distribution system near the Fawn Ridge Water Treatment Plant in Citrus Park damaged a 24-inch water main. Water service was shut down for about three hours. A precautionary boil-water notice covered the area west of the Veterans Expressway to Ehrlich Road and west of Gunn Highway to Racetrack Road, out to the Pinellas County line, mainly Westchase.

projects.name: Clearwater Coachman Park Water Main Strike
projects.description: Construction crews in Coachman Park accidentally hit a water main, cutting pressure to Clearwater Beach, Island Estates and parts of Sand Key and triggering a two-day boil-water advisory.
projects.detail: On Oct. 27, 2021, construction crews working in Clearwater's Coachman Park accidentally hit a water main. Customers on Clearwater Beach, Island Estates, parts of Sand Key and some downtown locations had low or no water pressure. The main was repaired that evening, but a precautionary boil-water advisory stayed in effect until it was lifted on Friday, Oct. 29.

projects.name: Fort Meade Fiber Install Water Main Break and Boil-Water Notice
projects.description: A contractor digging to install fiber-optic lines broke a Fort Meade water main and drained the city's water tower, and the repair was then held up by abandoned-in-place devices crews found underground.
projects.detail: On Sept. 8, 2026, a contractor digging to install fiber-optic lines in Fort Meade (Polk County) broke a main water pipe. The water loss drained the city's elevated water tower and set off a citywide boil-water advisory. A 14-inch valve linking the tower was to be replaced Sept. 17. That work could not be finished on schedule because of 'unforeseen field conditions associated with devices abandoned in place,' and engineering firm Woodard & Curran was brought in. The advisory was still in effect on Sept. 18 and was the city's fifth boil-water advisory of 2026.
projects.timeline: Sept 8, 2026 break → advisory still in effect Sept 18, 2026
